_notes.pages: Word-card choice: the book's only non-stopword ('a'/'the') content vocabulary is exactly 5 words -- cat, sat, on, cats, tip-top -- which map cleanly one-per-page in story order for pages 1-3 (cat/sat/on, each a genuinely new word on its page) and page 5 ('tip-top', the book's shouted finale word). Page 4 ('A cat on a cat on a cat!') introduces no new vocabulary at all -- it's pure cumulative repetition of 'cat'/'on' for comic effect, which is the book's own joke (the picture, not new text, carries the escalation). Rather than default to a duplicate 'cat' word card for page 4 (flat and non-distinct), 'cats' was assigned to page 4 instead of page 5: it is still in-book vocabulary (first printed on page 5, 'Tip-top cats!'), it is pedagogically apt for page 4's picture (three cats stacked -- the first clearly-plural scene), and it keeps all 5 word cards distinct for the three-part-cards / sequencing / match materials. 'tip-top' then stays on page 5 where it is actually printed.
_notes.sequencingDisplayOrder_matchDisplayOrder: Two different full derangements of [1,2,3,4,5] (no page's `order` value sits in its own position, position-by-position, in either list -- verified: seq=[2,1,4,5,3] vs identity [1,2,3,4,5] differs at every index; match=[5,3,1,2,4] vs identity differs at every index; seq vs match also differ at every index) -- so neither work sheet lets a row answer itself and rebuilds stay deterministic, per README.md step 2.
_notes.yesno: 10 items (5 true, 5 false) per the dp-the-sat.json / Jul-30 rollout convention (5/5 split, 'did the X sit?' phrasing). 5 true items are drawn straight from the book's own 5 pages (imageArt = p1.jpg..p5.jpg), one question per page, worded to describe exactly what that page's picture shows (single cat / cat sitting / two cats stacked / three cats stacked / four cats tip-top) so a teacher can visually verify book fidelity. 5 false items reuse the exact 'did the X sit?' phrasing on animals that never appear in this book (dog, pig, duck, owl, rabbit) -- clearly false since the-cat-sat's cast is a single cat, never any other animal -- via imageWord -> docs/picture-bank/photos/<word>/<word>.jpg (all 5 files verified present on disk before writing this JSON: dog/dog.jpg, pig/pig.jpg, duck/duck.jpg, owl/owl.jpg, rabbit/rabbit.jpg). Per the 2026-07-30 ruling, false-item words are NOT restricted to prior-week vocabulary -- picked for clear falseness relative to this specific book instead.
